entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-go
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-go

Release history of tramaj-go, the Go implementation, standard library only. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #go #tramaj-go

tramaj-go 0.1.0unreleased

Go port: parser, evaluator (concrete and symbolic modes), Node JSON codec, static analyses and a tramaj-go CLI. Standard library only, Go 1.21+.

  • added Hand-written port checked against `corpus/cases` by `corpus_test.go`: every case passes in both modes.
  • changed Breaking: numbers are two types, an integer and a float (decisions section 18). A literal and a JSON number are typed by their text: `3` is an integer, `3.0` and `3e0` are floats. Integers cover the signed 64-bit range; one outside it is a parse error as a literal and a `TypeMismatch` in the context.
  • changed Breaking: a number keeps its type when written. `str(1.0)` is `1.0` where it was `1`, and `CompactJSON` and `PrettyJSON` write a float with a fraction or an exponent.
  • changed Breaking: `eq` never equates an integer with a float, and `lt`/`lte`/`gt`/`gte` take two integers or two floats; a mixed pair is a `TypeMismatch`. An array index given to `has` or `lookup` is an integer.
  • changed Breaking: in a `tramaj.JSON` value an integer is an `int64` and a float a `float64`, where every number was a `float64`. `ParseJSON` types a number by its text and refuses none; `NormalizeNumbers` is what refuses an integer beyond 64 bits or a float too large for a double. `NumberLit` is now `IntLit` and `FloatLit`. New: `FormatInteger`, `FormatFloat`.
  • changed Breaking: `"$term"` is a reserved object key, and `int` and `float` replace `number` as v4 type primitives.
  • added The arithmetic profile: `sum`, `product`, `negate`, `quotient`, `inverse`, `floor-quotient`, `modulo`, `floor` and `real`, and the `NotRepresentable` error kind. It is off by default: `Options`, `DefaultOptions`, `EvalProgramWith` and `RunProgramWith` turn it on, and so does the CLI's `--arithmetic`.
  • added Terms: over a symbol an arithmetic builtin evaluates to `{"$term": op, "arguments": [...]}`, with its operands as written.
  • added `ArithmeticNames`, `ArithmeticOps` and `DeepArithmeticOps`, the arithmetic names a program references; `tramaj-go analyze arithmetic` prints them.
  • added `sort-by(list, fn)` and `sort-by-descending(list, fn)` (decisions section 20): a stable sort by a key function, over integer, float or string keys, strings by code point. Both are special forms lowered to one new AST constructor, `SortBy`, so neither name can be bound and called or passed by reference.
  • added `format-number(x, decimals, group)`: a number as positional decimal text, rounding its exact value with ties away from zero, 0 to 20 decimals, never an exponent or a negative zero. An ordinary builtin that needs no option.
  • added `round(x)`, the tenth name of the arithmetic profile: the nearest integer, ties away from zero. It builds a term over a symbol and is reported by `ArithmeticOps`.
entry.summary: Release history of `tramaj-go`, the Go implementation, standard library only.

entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-cli-rs
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-cli-rs

Release history of tramaj-cli-rs, the standalone Rust command-line interface over tramaj-rs. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #rust #tramaj-cli-rs

The unreleased entry has breaking changes to numbers: Migrating to integers and floats says what to do about each.

tramaj-cli-rs (none)unreleased

On the main branch after 0.1.0, not released yet: follows tramaj-rs to two number types, arithmetic, sorting and number formatting.

  • changed Breaking: numbers keep their type through the context and the output: `3` is an integer and `3.0` a float, and a whole-valued float is written with its fraction. An integer outside the signed 64-bit range is refused.
  • added `evaluate --arithmetic` turns the arithmetic profile on for the run. Without it, an error names the flag when the program references an arithmetic builtin.
  • added `analyze arithmetic` lists the arithmetic builtins a program and its libraries reference; `analyze all` carries the list under `arithmetic`.
  • added `sort-by`, `sort-by-descending` and `format-number` (decisions section 20) evaluate in every run, with no flag. `round` is the tenth arithmetic name: it needs `--arithmetic`, and `analyze arithmetic` reports it.

tramaj-cli-rs 0.1.02026-10-01

Rust port of tramaj-cli's Main.purs over the tramaj-rs crate.

  • added Template + JSON context evaluation and the `analyze` subcommands, as a single static binary.

entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-js
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-js

Release history of tramaj-js, the TypeScript implementation for Node.js and browsers. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #javascript #tramaj-js

The unreleased entry has breaking changes to numbers: Migrating to integers and floats says what to do about each.

tramaj-js 0.1.0unreleased

TypeScript port: parser, evaluator (concrete and symbolic modes), Node JSON codec and static analyses.

  • added Hand-written port checked against `corpus/cases` by `test/corpus.test.ts`.
  • added Object destructuring patterns in `@` bindings and lambda parameters (decisions section 17): a parser lowering to plain `Let`/`Lambda`, checked by shared corpus cases 100-118.
  • changed Breaking: numbers are two types, an integer and a float (decisions section 18). A literal and a JSON number are typed by their text: `3` is an integer, `3.0` and `3e0` are floats. Integers cover the guaranteed range, `-(2^53 - 1)` to `2^53 - 1`; one outside it is a parse error as a literal and a `TypeMismatch` in the context.
  • changed Breaking: a number keeps its type when written. `str(1.0)` is `1.0` where it was `1`, and every JSON boundary keeps a float a float.
  • changed Breaking: `eq` never equates an integer with a float, and `lt`/`lte`/`gt`/`gte` take two integers or two floats; a mixed pair is a `TypeMismatch`.
  • changed Breaking: the `Json` type gains `Float` and `bigint`. A plain `number` that is a safe integer is an integer and any other is a float; the float `3.0` is `new Float(3)`, and a result holds a `Float` for a whole-valued float. `isJsonObject` is false for a `Float`.
  • added `parseJson` and `stringify`, a JSON reader and writer that keep `3` and `3.0` apart, which `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify` do not; `float`, `isInteger`, `isFloat`, `numberValue`, `classifyNumber`, `normalizeNumbers`, `formatInteger` and `formatFloat`. `formatNumber` is removed.
  • changed Breaking: `"$term"` is a reserved object key, `int` and `float` replace `number` as v4 type primitives, and `nodeFromJson` rejects a number outside the value domain. In the AST, `IntLit` and `FloatLit` replace `NumberLit`, and `ScalarInt` and `ScalarFloat` replace `ScalarNum`; in `Value`, `int` and `float` replace `number`.
  • added The arithmetic profile: `sum`, `product`, `negate`, `quotient`, `inverse`, `floor-quotient`, `modulo`, `floor`, `real` and `round`, and the `NotRepresentable` error. It is off by default: `Options`, `defaultOptions`, `evalProgramWith` and `runProgramWith` turn it on. `round(x)` is the integer nearest to `x`, ties away from zero (decisions section 20).
  • added Terms: over a symbol an arithmetic builtin evaluates to `{"$term": op, "arguments": [...]}`, with its operands as written.
  • added `arithmeticNames`, `arithmeticOps` and `deepArithmeticOps`, the arithmetic names a program references.
  • added `sort-by(list, fn)` and `sort-by-descending(list, fn)` (decisions section 20) order a list by the key `fn` gives each element. Keys are all integers, all floats or all strings, compared by code point; anything else is a `TypeMismatch`, and a symbol or a term a `NotConcrete`. Both are stable, each on its own terms, and `fn` is applied once per element, in index order. They are core forms, in every profile.
  • added `format-number(x, decimals, group)` writes an integer or a float in positional decimal notation, with `decimals` digits (0 to 20) after the point and `group` between the groups of three digits of the integer part. It rounds the exact value of the number, ties away from zero, and never writes an exponent or a negative zero. An ordinary builtin, in every profile.
  • changed Breaking: `Expr` gains the constructor `SortBy` (`descending`, `collection`, `fn`), which `subExprs` and every analysis traverse. `sort-by` and `sort-by-descending` are special-form names, as `map` is: a program that bound one and called it now gets the form, or a parse error without exactly two arguments. `format-number` is a builtin name and `round` joins `arithmeticNames`; a program that binds either still shadows it.
  • added `emittedConstraintCount`, the number of constraints an evaluation emitted before equal ones are made one. It is there for tests, which have no other way to count the applications of a function.
entry.summary: Release history of `tramaj-js`, the TypeScript implementation for Node.js and browsers.

entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-py
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-py

Release history of tramaj-py, the Python implementation, standard library only. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #python #tramaj-py

The unreleased entry has breaking changes to numbers: Migrating to integers and floats says what to do about each.

tramaj-py (none)unreleased

On the main branch after 0.1.0, not released yet: two number types, arithmetic, sorting and number formatting.

  • changed Breaking: numbers are two types, an integer and a float (decisions section 18), and they are the two Python types: an `int` is an integer and a `float` a float, in the context and in the result. A literal and a JSON number are typed by their text: `3` is an integer, `3.0` and `3e0` are floats. Integers cover the signed 64-bit range; Python's own are unbounded, so one outside the range is refused and never rounded: a parse error as a literal, a `TypeMismatch` in the context, a `NotRepresentable` as a result.
  • changed Breaking: a number keeps its type when written. `str(1.0)` is `1.0` where it was `1`, and `compact_json`, `pretty_json` and the CLI write a float with a fraction or an exponent. `node_from_json` rejects an integer outside the range and a float too large for a double.
  • changed Breaking: `eq` never equates an integer with a float, and so neither does `json_equal`. `lt`/`lte`/`gt`/`gte` take two integers or two floats; a mixed pair is a `TypeMismatch`. An array index is an integer: `has` and `lookup` no longer take `1.0` for `1`.
  • changed Breaking: `int` and `float` are type primitives and `number` is no longer one (v4-types section 1). `"$term"` is a reserved object key, next to `"$sym"` and `"$type"`. `normalize_number` and `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are gone from `jsonval`; `VNumber` is replaced by `VInt` and `VFloat`.
  • added The arithmetic profile (reference section 11), ten builtins: `sum`, `product`, `negate`, `inverse`, `quotient`, `floor-quotient`, `modulo`, `floor`, `real` and `round`. It is an option of each evaluation, off by default: `run_program(..., arithmetic=True)`, and `--arithmetic` on the command line. Without it the ten names are unbound. `round` (decisions section 20) gives the nearest integer, ties away from zero, unlike Python's own.
  • added Terms: over a symbol an arithmetic builtin builds `{"$term": op, "arguments": [...]}` with its operands as written (v3-symbols section 1.9), and a well-formed term can be seeded back in symbolic mode.
  • added `arithmetic_ops` and `deep_arithmetic_ops`, the scope-aware analysis of which arithmetic names a program references free; `python -m tramaj analyze arithmetic` prints the deep one. `parse_json` reads JSON text with each number typed by its text. The `NotRepresentable` error kind.
  • added The corpus runner declares `int-float`, `arithmetic`, `int64`, `sort`, `format-number` and `round`, and turns arithmetic on only for the cases that list it.
  • added `sort-by(list, fn)` and `sort-by-descending(list, fn)` (decisions section 20): a stable sort by key, in every profile. The key function runs once per element, in index order; the keys of one call are all integers, all floats or all strings, and strings compare by code point.
  • changed Breaking: `sort-by` and `sort-by-descending` are special-form names lowering to one new AST constructor, `ast.SortBy`. A program can no longer bind one and call it as an ordinary name, and a wrong argument count is a parse error.
  • added `format-number(x, decimals, group)` (decisions section 20), an ordinary builtin of every profile: positional decimal text with 0 to 20 decimals and an optional group separator. It rounds the exact value of the number, ties away from zero, on `fractions.Fraction`, and never writes an exponent or a negative zero.

tramaj-py 0.1.02026-09-27

Python port: parser, evaluator (concrete and symbolic modes), Node JSON codec, static analyses and a python -m tramaj CLI. Standard library only, Python 3.9+.

  • added Hand-written port checked against `corpus/cases` by `tests/test_corpus.py`: every case passes in both modes.
  • added Object destructuring patterns in `@` bindings and lambda parameters (decisions section 17): a parser lowering to plain `Let`/`Lambda`, checked by shared corpus cases 100-118.
entry.summary: Release history of `tramaj-py`, the Python implementation, standard library only.

entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-rs
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-rs

Release history of tramaj-rs, the Rust implementation of the parser, evaluator and analyses. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #rust #tramaj-rs

The unreleased entry has breaking changes to numbers: Migrating to integers and floats says what to do about each.

tramaj-rs (none)unreleased

On the main branch after 0.1.0, not released yet: two number types, arithmetic, sorting and number formatting.

  • changed Breaking: numbers are two types, an integer and a float (decisions section 18): `Value::Int` and `Value::Float`, `Expr::IntLit` and `Expr::FloatLit`. A literal or a JSON number with neither a fraction nor an exponent is an integer. Nothing converts between the two: `eq(1, 1.0)` is false, `lt` and its siblings refuse a mixed pair, an index is an integer, and `str(1.0)` is `1.0`.
  • changed Breaking: the integer range is the signed 64-bit one. A literal outside it is a parse error and a context number outside it a `TypeMismatch`; neither is rounded. A float too large for a double is refused the same way.
  • changed Breaking: JSON goes in and out as `tramaj_rs::json::Json`, not `serde_json::Value`: `run_program`, `eval_program` and `Node` take and return it. `json::parse` types a number by its text and `json::stringify` writes an integer as digits and a float with a fraction or an exponent. `json::from_serde` and `json::to_serde` bridge to `serde_json`.
  • changed Breaking: the type primitives `int` and `float` replace `number`, and `"$term"` is a reserved key: a parse error as an object key, a `TypeMismatch` in a context.
  • added The arithmetic profile: `sum`, `product`, `negate`, `quotient`, `inverse`, `floor-quotient`, `modulo`, `floor` and `real`, and the `NotRepresentable` error. It is off by default: `Options`, `eval_program_with` and `run_program_with` turn it on.
  • added Terms: over a symbol an arithmetic builtin evaluates to `{"$term": op, "arguments": [...]}`, with its operands as written.
  • added `arithmetic_ops` and `deep_arithmetic_ops`, the arithmetic names a program references.
  • added `round(x)`, the tenth name of the arithmetic profile (decisions section 20): the integer nearest to a float, a tie going away from zero, and a `NotRepresentable` outside the 64-bit range. Over a symbol it builds a term like the other nine, a seeded `round` term is accepted, and `arithmetic_ops` reports it. `ARITHMETIC_NAMES` has ten names.
  • added `sort-by(list, fn)` and `sort-by-descending(list, fn)`: two special forms over one new constructor, `Expr::SortBy`. A stable sort by the key a function gives each element, applied once per element in index order. The keys of one call are all integers, all floats or all strings, compared by code point; anything else is a `TypeMismatch`, a symbol or a term a `NotConcrete`. Every analysis sees the collection and the key function. No profile is needed.
  • added `format-number(x, decimals, group)`, an ordinary builtin of every profile: a number in positional decimal notation, with 0 to 20 decimals and a separator between groups of three digits. It rounds the exact value of the number, a tie going away from zero, and never writes an exponent or a negative zero.
  • changed Breaking: `sort-by` and `sort-by-descending` are special-form names: a program can no longer bind one and call it, a wrong argument count is a parse error, and so is either name passed by reference. `Expr` has a new variant, and `format-number` is in `builtin_names`.
  • added `eval::emitted_constraint_count`: how many constraints an evaluation emitted before equal ones are made one. It exists for the test that a sort applies its key function once per element, which no program can observe.

tramaj-rs 0.1.02026-10-01

Hand-written port kept in agreement with the other implementations through the shared conformance corpus.

  • added Parser, AST, evaluator and static analyses, plus a program-card analysis.
  • added Serde-based Node JSON codec.
  • added Object destructuring patterns in `@` bindings and lambda parameters (decisions section 17): a parser lowering to plain `Let`/`Lambda`, checked by shared corpus cases 100-118.
entry.summary: Release history of `tramaj-rs`, the Rust implementation of the parser, evaluator and analyses.

entry.title: Changelog: tramaj-hs
entry.content:
Changelog: tramaj-hs

Release history of tramaj-hs, the Haskell implementation, also the engine behind Kitchen-Sink’s templating sections. Releases happen when there are major changes rather than on a schedule; each entry below is one version. Every implementation has its own page like this one, and each page is tagged so the site builds one Atom feed per implementation: #changelog #haskell #tramaj-hs

The unreleased entry has breaking changes to numbers: Migrating to integers and floats says what to do about each.

tramaj-hs (none)unreleased

On the main branch after 0.3.0.0, not released yet: two number types and arithmetic.

  • changed Breaking: numbers are two types, an integer and a float (decisions section 18). A literal and a JSON number are typed by their text: `3` is an integer, `3.0` and `3e0` are floats. Integers cover the signed 64-bit range; one outside it is a parse error as a literal and a `TypeMismatch` in the context.
  • changed Breaking: a number keeps its type when written. `str(1.0)` is `1.0` where it was `1`, and every JSON boundary writes a float with a fraction or an exponent.
  • changed Breaking: `eq` never equates an integer with a float, and `lt`/`lte`/`gt`/`gte` take two integers or two floats; a mixed pair is a `TypeMismatch`.
  • changed Breaking: `Tramaj.Json` replaces `Data.Aeson.Value` in the public API, with `JInt` and `JFloat`; `fromAeson` and `toAeson` bridge the two.
  • changed Breaking: `"$term"` is a reserved object key, and `int` and `float` replace `number` as v4 type primitives.
  • added The arithmetic profile: `sum`, `product`, `negate`, `quotient`, `inverse`, `floor-quotient`, `modulo`, `floor` and `real`, and the `NotRepresentable` error. It is off by default: `Options`, `defaultOptions`, `evalProgramWith` and `runProgramWith` turn it on.
  • added Terms: over a symbol an arithmetic builtin evaluates to `{"$term": op, "arguments": [...]}`, with its operands as written.
  • added `arithmeticOps` and `deepArithmeticOps`, the arithmetic names a program references.

tramaj-hs 0.3.0.0date not recorded

Implements v2 of the language: a rewrite of the semantic core, not an extension of it.

  • changed Documents are expressions: `Element` and `Fragment` are ordinary `Expr` constructors; the separate template-phase AST and `JsonProgram` are gone.
  • added `Tramaj.Node`, the normative interchange format, with an encoder and a strict decoder.
  • added `Tramaj.Analysis`: static import names, action keys, context holes, context reads and unsupplied params, with deep variants.
  • changed Imports take their parameters three ways (expression, `ctx(path)`, or later call); `partial-import` is gone.
  • changed `a <> b` concatenation, lazy `branch`, `adapt-actions`, `.(a, b)` fragments, string escapes, object shorthand, builtins as values.
  • fixed Malformed `action(...)`/`value(...)` in an element argument no longer backtracks into a meaningless `Call`; a backtick in a static string position is reported.

tramaj-hs 0.2.0.0date not recorded

Adds a JSON-producing mode for hosts that want the data half of the language on its own.

  • added `Tramaj.Ast.JsonProgram`, `Tramaj.Parser.parseJsonProgram` and `Tramaj.Eval.evalJsonProgram`.

tramaj-hs 0.1.0.0date not recorded

Initial release, extracted from the repository it was written in.

  • added Ports the PureScript package's `Tramaj.Ast` / `Tramaj.Parser` / `Tramaj.Eval` to megaparsec + aeson.
entry.summary: Release history of `tramaj-hs`, the Haskell implementation, also the engine behind Kitchen-Sink's templating sections.
